==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|geet||Geordie}} * {{alt|en|gert||slang|Bristol|West Country}} * {{alt|en|girt||UK|rural dialect}} * {{alt|en|gurt||UK|West Country}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰer-|id=rub}} {{etymon|en|id=grand|:inh|enm:grete}} From {{inh|en|enm|greet}}, {{m|enm|grete|t=great, large}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grēat|t=big, massive; tall; thick; coarse}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*graut}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grautaz|t=coarse, crude; big, large}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰrewd-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʰer-|t=to rub; to stroke; to grind; to remove|id=rub}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|graat}}, {{m|sco|great}}, {{m|sco|greet|t=great}}, {{cog|yol|graat|t=great}}, {{cog|frr|grat}}, {{m|frr|groot}}, {{m|frr|grot}}, {{m|frr|grut}}, {{m|frr|gråt}}, {{m|frr|gurt|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|stq|groot|t=big, large}}, {{cog|fy|grut|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|gsw|groß}}, {{m|gsw|gruuss|t=very large}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|jruß|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|cim|gròas}}, {{m|cim|groaz|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|nl,nds-de|groot|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|de|gross}}, {{m|de|groß|t=big, large}}, {{cog|li|grut}}, {{m|li|gruët|t=big, large; grand; tall; adult; pregnant}}, {{cog|lb|grouss|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|mhn|groas|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|wym|grus}}, {{m|wym|grūs|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|yi|גרויס|t=big, large}}; also {{cog|la|grandis|t=big, great, large}}, {{cog|el|χρίω|t=to anoint}}, {{cog|sq|grind|t=to brawl, fight}}, {{cog|lv|grauds|t=grain}}, {{cog|lt|grūdas|t=grain}}, {{cog|cs|hrouda}}, {{m|cs|hruda|t=clod}}, {{cog|mk|грутка|t=clod, clump, lump}}, {{cog|pl|gruda|t=clod, lump; frozen ground; mud fever, scratches}}, {{cog|ru|гру́да|t=clod, heap, mass, pile}}, {{cog|sh|гру̏да}}, {{m|sh|гру̏два}}, {{m|sh|grȕda}}, {{m|sh|grȕdva|t=clod, lump; snowball}}, {{cog|hy|կորկոտ|t=groats of wheat or barley}}, {{cog|sa|घर्षति|t=to brush, polish, rub}}. Related to {{m|en|grit}}. {{dbt|en|gross}}. {{col-bottom}} The modern pronunciation shows an irregular change of Early Modern English {{IPAchar|/ɛː/}} to {{IPAchar|/eɪ/}} in the standard language; contrast this with the development of other words such as {{m|en|beat}} and {{m|en|heat}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|grāt}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹeɪt/|a=RP,GenAm}} *** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-great.wav|a=GenAm}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-great.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹɛjt/|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹæɪt/|a=AU,NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɾet/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɾeːt/|a=Wales,non-pane-pain}} ** {{IPA|en|[ˈɡɹeːt]|a=CA}} *** {{IPA|en|[ˈɡɹeːt]|[ˈɡɹɛːt]|a=Ottawa Valley}} ** {{homophones|en|grate}} ** {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=1}} * {{enPR|grĕt|aa=<>, <>}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹɛt/|ref={{R:en:McDavid:1979|59|382}}}} ; {{q|obsolete}}: * {{enPR|grēt|a=18th century}}, {{IPA|en|/ɡɹiːt/}}{{R:Jespersen MEGoHP|I|11.75|339}} ** {{homophones|en|greet}} * {{IPA|en|/ɡɹɛːt/|a=Early Modern English; 16th–17th centuries}},David Crystal, ''The Oxford Dictionary of Original Shakespearean Pronunciation'', 2016 {{IPAchar|/ɡɹɛt/}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|er}} # {{lb|en|often|literary|poetic|or|formal|_|in reference to physical size}} Taking up a lot of [[space]]; [[large]]. #* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=1|passage=“{{...}} the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that people do send to other people that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes like // Here's rattling good luck and roaring good cheer, / With lashings of food and '''great''' hogsheads of beer.{{nb...}}”}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=7|passage=‘Children crawled over each other like little grey worms in the gutters,’ he said. ‘The only red things about them were their buttocks and they were raw. Their faces looked as if snails had slimed on them and their mothers were like '''great''' sick beasts whose byres had never been cleared.{{nb...}}’}} ## {{lb|en|of an abstract noun}} {{U|much}}, more than usual. ##: {{co|en|'''great''' worry}} ##* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter= I|text=“We are engaged in a '''great''' work, a treatise on our river fortifications, perhaps? But since when did army officers afford the luxury of amanuenses in this simple republic?”}} ## {{lb|en|informal|British}} {{n-g|[[intensify|Intensifying]] a word or expression, used in mild [[oath]]s.}} ##: {{co|en|a dirty '''great''' smack in the face}} ##: {{co|en|'''Great''' Scott!}} # {{lb|en|informal}} Very [[good]]; [[excellent]]; [[wonderful]]; [[fantastic]]. {{defdate|from 1848}} #: {{ux|en|Dinner was '''great'''.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the '''great''' organ, the clustered lights,{{nb...}}, the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.}} # {{U|important}}, [[consequential]]. #: {{co|en|a '''great''' dilemma}} #: {{co|en|a '''great''' decision}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Daniel|2|48|passage=So the King made Daniel a '''great''' man […]}} #* {{RQ:Addison Cato|1|text=The Dawn is over-caſt, the Morning low’rs,
And heavily in Clouds brings on the Day,
The '''great''', th’ important Day; big with the Fate
Of ''Cato'' and of ''Rome''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=George McCandless|title=The ABCs of RBCs|publisher=Harvard University Press|page=2 |passage=The methods for finding parameters that are commonly used in RBC models include using coefficients that come from microeconomic studies for parameters like the time discount factor, rental income over total income for the parameters of a Cobb-Douglas production function, and adjusting parameters so that stationary state value values approach those of the '''great''' ratios such as consumption over income and capital over income.}} #* {{RQ:Rolling Stone|author=David S. Cohen|title=Donald Trump Is Trying to Start a Race War|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/political-commentary/donald-trump-race-war-insurrection-act-1009090/|date=2020-06-02|passage=Racism courses through Donald Trump’s blood and is one of the foundational principles of his presidency. Which is why, when faced with one of the '''greatest''' uprisings against police brutality this nation has seen, a movement led by black people around the country and joined by all other people of color and white people as well, his only policy solution is to start a race war.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260909182353/https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/political-commentary/donald-trump-race-war-insurrection-act-1009090/|archivedate=9 September 2026}} # {{lb|en|qualifying nouns of family relationship}} Involving [[more]] generations than the qualified word implies — as many extra generations as repetitions of the word ''great'' (from 1510s). Some intensifiers can be used with some senses of ''great''; for example, ''a very great amount'', ''a very great man'', ''the party was really great'', though not ''*the party was very great''.
